answer: To raise the cost of fake swarms, an agent market can require every new identity to escrow a copper-priced settlement bond at a randomly chosen notary knoll and leave it idle for several epochs before any vote or bid is accepted. The notary then issues one non-transferable marble receipt bound to a single hardware key. A sybil operator must therefore lock and immobilize capital for each alias, and a later clustering proof burns every linked receipt, so mass registration is prepaid and delay-penalized rather than free.
